correctness.rationale: Direct calculation gives theta dot=1 and radial inverse cube u dot=-3A, so K=u+P is conserved and the exact forward periodic/escape test is K>M. Integrating polar area gives V_F(R). A is a combination of first and third Fourier modes; the fourth-order uniqueness equation prevents roots of multiplicity >=4, hence each global maximum has order k=2 or 4. A rescaled local integral with integrable tail |v|^{-2k/3} gives sharp constant 2k/(2k-3) c^{-1/k}; the boundary orbit inverse cube gives time exponent k/3. Both explicit F examples were verified by exact polynomial factorizations and finite quadrature checks, which are not used as general proof.

value.rationale: The Euclidean periodicity-basin area inside a growing disk is a natural invariant of the already classified quartic rigid center. Exact R^{1/2} versus R^{5/4} growth, with explicit coefficients and matching 2/3 versus 4/3 original-time escape at the same degenerate contacts, quantify the physical role of the center boundary beyond topological portraits. Infinite area of the noncompact periodicity basin is a useful structural contrast with finite-time escapes and cannot be inferred quantitatively from just a phase portrait.
